subject: Scenario ledger — platform fit comparison + credit vs commitment tradeoffs
messages:
From: Elliot Gould <elliot@bridgeway.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@acmetech.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — evaluating alternatives for inference stack

Hannah / Connor,

Thanks for the initial call yesterday. Procurement asked me to get a simple A/B ledger showing the delta between sticking with our incumbent (CloudForge) vs moving to Redwood. They want to see both: (1) one-time migration credits/assistance you can offer and (2) what a committed-usage discount profile looks like over 12 months.

Can you send a short scorecard (cost, expected latency delta, integration effort, audit/compliance items) and highlight any hard constraints (eg: minimum commit, lead time for Dedicated pool, data residency options)? Maya wants to review before Friday.

Also: we run inference for customer-facing chat and real-time embeddings for search — latency matter more than absolute $/token for us.

Best,
Elliot

--
Elliot Gould
Head of ML Platforms, Bridgeway Labs
elliot@bridgeway.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Gould <elliot@bridgeway.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — evaluating alternatives for inference stack

Elliot —

Attaching a compact scorecard and our updated offer (redwood_offer_v2.pdf). Quick notes up front:

- Migration assistance: we can provide a one-time professional-services credit of $75k aimed at runtime compatibility and KV-cache migration (applies to Dedicated migrations only).
- Commit vs credit: 12-month commit discounts scale at 20% (base), 28% (mid), 35% (high) depending on committed vCPU/GPU hours — detailed tiers in the PDF.
- Latency: for your chat/embeddings workload we expect median token latency to be ~10–15% lower on our Dedicated NPU pool vs CloudForge with similar quantized models (we've benchmarked with a 512-token median), but we also recommend an initial pilot to profile your prompt mix.
- Compliance: Private VPC + KMS options available; SOC2 evidence folder link in the PDF.

I've also attached an alternatives spreadsheet that scores technical fit and migration risk. Connor — can you add an estimated on-ramp timeline (weeks) for a 3-node Dedicated pool and a playbook for prefix cache cutover?

Thanks,
Hannah

Attachments: redwood_offer_v2.pdf (15KB stub), Acme_Tech_alternatives_scorecard.xlsx (34KB stub)

--
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Gould <elliot@bridgeway.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — evaluating alternatives for inference stack

Elliot / Hannah —

Quick timeline estimate from infra/ops:
- Pilot (1–2 nodes Dedicated): 3 weeks (provisioning + smoke tests + perf sweep)
- Full 3-node Dedicated on-prem-ready pool: 6–8 weeks (includes networking and cert wiring)
- KV/prefix cache cutover playbook: ~2 days of coordinated cutover during low-traffic window (we'll stage with traffic shadowing).

Operational caveats: if you need strict <50ms P95 for 512-token calls we may recommend hybrid routing (hosted low-latency endpoints + Dedicated for throughput). That changes economics a bit — Hannah, see the scenario labeled "hybrid" in the spreadsheet.

Connor

--
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

From: Maya Patel <maya@acmetech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Elliot Gould <elliot@bridgeway.ai>
Date: 2027-04-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scenario ledger — platform fit comparison + credit vs commitment tradeoffs

Hannah/Connor,

Thanks — scored the spreadsheet quickly and a few clarifying asks before we loop procurement:
1) The $75k migration credit — does it apply if we do a staged migration (pilot then phased migration) or only on a single go-live?
2) On commit tiers: is the commit upfront or monthly true-up? We want flexibility in Q3 if volume spikes.
3) Any guest limits / user-seat constraints tied to the credits?

Procurement is especially sensitive to guaranteed rollback windows and liability during the initial 30 days. If you can put a short blurb on rollback assistance and an SLA exception process, that would help.

Maya

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acmetech.com>, Elliot Gould <elliot@bridgeway.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scenario ledger — platform fit comparison + credit vs commitment tradeoffs

Maya —

Answers inline and next steps:

1) Migration credit scope: the $75k credit can be consumed across a staged migration (pilot + phased migration) as long as the work is invoiced within the 90-day onboarding window. We'll itemize deliverables (pilot validation, KV transfer, cutover support).

2) Commit mechanics: we offer both upfront commit and monthly true-up options. Upfront commit gives the highest discount (35% at top tier); monthly true-up still gets tiered discounts but with a 6% haircut relative to the equivalent upfront commit band. We can model a blended Q3 cushion — see the "commit-flex" column in the PDF.

3) Guest / seat limits: no hidden per-seat gating on throughput credits. Credits apply to token usage and PS line items only. Operational seats for console/ops are separate and can be included as an add-on.

Rollback & SLA exceptions: we will draft a 1-paragraph rollback assistance clause for Procurement that includes a 30-day support runway, defined rollback checkpoints, and an optional short-term SLA uplift during onboarding (applies to Dedicated). Lauren — can you draft the clause and a short amendment for review?

Next steps:
- I will upload the updated PDF with commit-flex examples and rollback blurb by EOD tomorrow.
- Connor will add the pilot runbook appendix to the scorecard.
- Elliot/Maya: if you share the approximate Q2 token runway we can produce a simple cost toggle sheet showing blended monthly vs upfront outcomes.

Thanks,
Hannah

Attachments referenced: Acme_Tech_alternatives_scorecard.xlsx, redwood_offer_v2.pdf

--
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
